notes.text:
Two things checked on 2026-08-28 that bear on the direction:

**1. This is not specific to this repo, and it is not new.** pipao-v2's `claude-bg` attempts have the
same shape: no `session_id`/`transcript_path` on any row, and zero entries in `.kanban/nudges/`.
Both hkb hooks return immediately without `KB_TASK` (`src/hook.js:32` for PreToolUse, `:158` for
Stop), so on both boards **hkb's permission policy has never run in a worker** — the only thing
governing workers has been Claude Code's native `--allowedTools` matching.

That has a consequence for #112/#124: the pilot's terminal-verb denials cannot have come from
`firstWords`, because the hook that calls it was inert. #124 fixed a real bug in hkb's function, but
the live failure the workers hit was most likely Claude Code's own compound-command matching against
`--allowedTools` — which needs one live test to confirm, and a different fix if so.

**2. A hook-free route exists for the session fields.** `claude agents --json` exposes `id`,
`sessionId` and `cwd` per background agent, and the dispatcher already holds the agent id — it stops
the agent by id when it reaps. Resolving `session_id` (and from it `transcript_path`) **in the
dispatcher** on the tick after launch, or at reap, needs no env passthrough and no hook. `claude
agents --json` is already called every tick, so it is free.

So the fix splits: session fields → dispatcher-side, from `claude agents`; the nudge → still needs
`KB_TASK` in the session, for which the cheapest fallback is deriving it from the worktree name the
launch already sets (`kb-{n}-{k}`, `src/board.js:30`) when the env is absent. Both halves want the
`hkb doctor` line the card asks for.

## The graph ```mermaid graph BT A["#132 dispatcher records the session
from claude agents --json
src/dispatch.js · src/model.js"] B["#133 hooks derive the task
from the worktree name
src/hook.js · src/board.js"] C["#134 doctor warns, docs say
what each profile really runs
src/doctor.js · docs/harnesses.md"] R["#125 verify + synthesize
incl. the live test that settles #112"] C --> A C --> B R --> C ``` Arrows point from a task to what blocks it. | task | blocked by | paths | why it is its own PR | |---|---|---|---| | #132 | — | `src/dispatch.js`, `src/model.js`, `test/jobs.test.js` | hook-free: the listing is already fetched every tick; only the write is new | | #133 | — | `src/hook.js`, `src/board.js`, `test/session.test.js`, `test/permission.test.js` | the hooks' gate, nothing else | | #134 | #132, #133 | `src/doctor.js`, `test/doctor.test.js`, `docs/harnesses.md`, `README.md` | can only describe what shipped | | #125 | #134 | — | one real attempt end to end, plus the #112 live test | Invariants: - **#132 and #133 are independent and path-disjoint.** They converge on the *same rows* through the same `SESSION_FIELDS`/`sessionUpdate` and the same `.kanban/sessions/-` marker — that contract is written into both bodies, because neither worker can see the other's. `src/model.js` is given to #132 alone and `src/board.js` to #133 alone so they never touch one file. - **The root is blocked by the only leaf**, #134. - **Not a track**: two genuinely parallel children. Decided here, so it is not relitigated: **env stays authoritative** in #133; the worktree name is a fallback, never an override. And the #112 question — whether the pilot's denials were Claude Code's native allowlist matching rather than hkb's inert hook — is settled by a live test in the root's verify pass, not by inference. Correction recorded for honesty: #134 was briefly claimed with its links inverted (my `hkb link` argument order), blocked back to *todo* within a minute, and relinked. Its first attempt row shows that; it is not a failure of the task.

Evidence for step 3 of the verify pass: #138 quotes the denial text a real `claude` worker received for `cd`, `export`, `VAR=… cmd` and a `while` loop — *"Permission to use Bash has been denied because Claude Code is running in don't ask mode"*. That is Claude Code's native message, not hkb's. Whether native also denies an allowed command with a heredoc containing `|`/`;` (the exact #112 shape) is being measured by the a-vs-b workflow's `heredoc-compound` probe; use its result rather than re-running the test if it lands first.

**Step 3 of the verify pass — the answer is in, measured, and it is not the heredoc.**

An adversarial workflow (11 agents, 2026-08-28, Claude Code 2.1.250) read all 71 worker transcripts on this board and reproduced the failure in a throwaway repo:

- **86 refusals in 29 worktrees are Claude Code's `--worktree` isolation guard**, triggered by the bash-builtin *name* `complete` anywhere in the command — *"runs a string through complete, which can't be verified to stay inside the worktree"*. Every spelling: `hkb complete …`, `--summary-file`, even `node bin/hkb.js complete`. No heredoc needed. `hkb block` is never refused. A PreToolUse `allow` does **not** override this guard.
- The heredoc/prefix denial (an allowed `Bash(hkb *)` prefix with `|`/`;` in a heredoc body is denied natively) is real but accounts for **2** cases.
- `firstWords` (#112/#124) accounts for **zero**: hkb's hook never ran in a bg worker.

So for the live test: if your terminal verb is refused, look at the refusal text. If it names the worktree guard, that is the known cause — file nothing new, cite this comment, and finish via the route workers already use (a `.mjs` under `$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/` spawning `hkb` with a literal argv). The proposed fix is an alias without the token — `hkb finish` — being measured now.

residual_risk: Every permission measurement is Claude Code 2.1.250/2.1.251 on this host. The guard could change or be absent elsewhere, in which case the alias is harmless but the docs' emphasis would overstate a build-specific quirk. docs/harnesses.md dates and versions the table so a reader can re-check rather than trust it.

The fix is inert until merged AND the global hkb is refreshed: the Stop hook runs `hkb hook stop`, which resolves to the main checkout, so a worker on today's install still reads the old `hkb complete` nudge. Verified: the nudge that fired at me printed the old text.

#137's tick-stamping is still unproven in production — I could not observe it because the running dispatcher predates it (#140). Its unit tests pass, but no attempt on this board has been stamped by that path.

The doctor rates clause fires per background profile with sessions; a board with several such profiles and no rates repeats it on each line. Deliberate (each line answers about its own profile) but it is repetition.

The wiki keeps only the one paragraph this change touches, unstamped. Five pages were already stale for #124/#127/#131 drift this task did not re-verify, and stamping would have blessed claims it did not read — /repolore:refresh is still owed from #134.
verification: npm run smoke — 25 content checks, 3 command checks, 9 init checks (templates and the skill are read from the package at runtime)
node --test test/doctor.test.js — 48 pass, including #134's two fixture-board warnings and 3 new cases
node bin/hkb.js doctor — all green on this board, now printing the stats.rates clause
live permission probes from inside this worker: heredoc vs --note control, herestring, < redirect, backslash continuation, two-line command, bare `complete`, quoted `complete`, `source`, $(…)
node bin/hkb.js finish 999999 --from-stdin < payload.json — ran end to end with | ; && in the payload, and queued canonically as `complete`
session coverage tallied over all 89 attempts on the board by driving fetchBoard/loadRun directly
observed the Stop hook live: .kanban/nudges/125-1 = 1, .kanban/sessions/125-1 written, session_id + transcript_path on the row mid-attempt

results.summary:
The verify pass found that the four PRs left one thing broken that none of them could see: a claude-bg worker cannot type the command the protocol asks it for. Fixed here (PR #142), with the #112 question settled by measurement.

## 1. A fresh claude-bg attempt (this one) — the chain works, end to end

KB_TASK undefined; CLAUDE_JOB_DIR and CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID set. After a deliberate stop: .kanban/nudges/125-1 = 1 (the hook found the attempt from the kb-125-1 checkout with no env and blocked the stop), .kanban/sessions/125-1 holds the session id, and the row carried session_id 943fa290-fb54-48da-af8e-edb4f2b42cbc and transcript_path MID-ATTEMPT — stamped by the Stop hook's recordSessions, before any terminal verb. Better than #135's card claimed: the row was priceable and resumable while still running.

A price: there is none, and there cannot be. hkb stats reports 244 turns · in 488 · out 207k · cache 656k written / 37M read (3 transcripts) and no money, because .kanban/board.json has no stats.rates — and doctor said `✓ session recorded on 3/8` and stopped, which reads as spend visibility working. Fixed: sessionFinding now appends the missing half (see 6).

## 2. Session coverage across all 89 attempts, and #132/#137 has never fired

claude/completed 3/55 · protocol_violation 0/10 · timed_out 0/5 · crashed 0/2 · blocked 0/5 · claude-track/completed 0/1. The three stamped rows are #115-1, #132-3, #134-2 — every attempt that ran a terminal verb after #135 merged (12:31), and no others.

So #135 works and #137's tick-stamping has never executed on this board: the `hkb dispatch --loop 60` that launched this attempt at 13:02 has been running since 06:13, hours before #137 merged at 12:46, and a long-running loop keeps the code it imported at startup even though the global hkb symlinks into the checkout. Filed as #140 (the loop should give itself up on upgrade — exit 4 already means exactly that — or doctor should say it). Not patched here: restarting the dispatcher is its own change.

## 3. #112 SETTLED — and it was never about | ; &&

Measured from this live worker, Claude Code 2.1.250/2.1.251:

  RUNS:  heartbeat --note "…" · the same command with <<<'…' (herestring) · with < /dev/null · split over two lines · with a \ continuation · `echo complete` inside quotes · --grep=complete
  DENIED: any command with a <<'EOF' heredoc — "Permission to use Bash has been denied because Claude Code is running in don't ask mode" — INCLUDING a heredoc whose body has no metacharacters at all
  DENIED: `node bin/hkb.js complete` with no arguments, and bare `echo complete` — "This session is isolated in the worktree …, but this command runs a string through complete, which can't be verified to stay inside the worktree"
  RUNS:  `node bin/hkb.js block` and `request-review`

Control that settles it: heartbeat --note "…" is allowed and the identical heartbeat with a metacharacter-free heredoc is denied. The heredoc is refused for its SHAPE, whatever it contains — so the pilot's failure was never about | ; && in the payload, and #124 did not fail to fix it because there was nothing there for hkb to fix. And `complete` is refused because it is a bash builtin (complete -C <cmd> runs a string): the guard matches an argument token equal to it, so no quoting helps (`node bin/hkb.js "complete"` is refused too). `source` is refused identically. $(…) command substitution is also refused.

Consequence: on the default profile the two shapes prescribed for FINISHING were the two a worker could not run, so it stalled and the dispatcher wrote it off — 10 protocol_violations on this board against 5 timeouts and 2 crashes.

## 4. The fix — `hkb finish`

`finish` is `complete` under a name no shell claims, resolved in main() before routing, so the run record, the outbox replay (terminalArgv) and the board still say `complete`. Everything a worker reads now names finish and prescribes a file redirect instead of a heredoc: the worker prompt, the track runner's prompt, the Stop hook's nudge (which had been telling a stalling worker to run the one command it could not), SKILL.md, protocol.md, the Copilot agent template, README, and templates/doc-section.md which generates CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md. block and request-review are not builtins and keep one name each. docs/harnesses.md gains the measurement table under "Which layer is actually enforcing".

Proof: in this same session, `node bin/hkb.js finish` reaches hkb's own usage error, and `node bin/hkb.js finish 999999 --from-stdin < payload.json` (payload containing | ; &&) executed end to end. This card was completed with it.

## 5. doctor — ok here, warns on a fixture

`node bin/hkb.js doctor` is all-green on this board; node --test test/doctor.test.js is 48 pass, including #134's two fixture-board warning cases and three new ones here.

## 6. Second seam fixed — recorded but unpriceable

sessionFinding gained a `priced` argument: with sessions recorded and no stats.rates it appends "· no `stats.rates` in .kanban/board.json, so those transcripts give `hkb stats` turns and tokens but never a cost". Still an ok (an unconfigured rates table is a fact, not a broken board), silent when rates exist, silent when nothing is recorded yet.

## Also filed

#140 — a dispatch --loop never picks up an upgrade (above).
#141 — "Could not resolve to an Issue with the number of N" matches the `could not resolve` DNS pattern in src/gh.js:30, so a missing issue is classed as network and a terminal verb for it is queued to the outbox to be replayed forever. Reproduced; exit 0 and a "we'll do it later" message for a write that was dropped.

## For the next worker

The alias does nothing until this merges AND the global hkb is refreshed: the Stop hook runs `hkb hook stop`, which resolves to the main checkout, so the nudge I triggered still printed the old `hkb complete` text. After merge, restart the dispatcher loop too — that is #140, and it is why #137 has never run.

One small gap hit while filing #140/#141 and not fixed: `hkb create` takes --body inline only, so on a shell-vetting harness a long body needs a spawn helper with a literal argv. --body-file would close it.
